26-## Stability
27-
28:New releases come out many times a day, but the install command below gives you the **stable channel**: a release reaches it only after the full test suite and a two-hour, 600,000-page load test pass on that exact release, and only when an important fix is waiting or stable is a week old. Updates are never installed without your say-so unless you turn on automatic upgrades. After an upgrade, gbrain shows a one-time notice listing what changed in behaviour. Stable also comes with a written promise about which commands, flags, tools, config keys and output fields stay the same, and how much warning you get before one changes. [docs/STABILITY.md](docs/STABILITY.md) explains that promise, how often stable moves, how to pin a version or go back, and what the faster alpha channel is for.
29-
30-## Install
31-
--
38-> gbrainio workspace new         # pick a plan in the browser
39-> curl -fsSL https://bun.sh/install | bash   # skip if Bun 1.4.4+ is installed
40-> export PATH="$HOME/.bun/bin:$PATH"
41:> bun install -g github:garrytan/gbrain#stable   # the gbrain CLI only; no local brain
42-> # Claude Code (an existing gbrain entry is kept):
43-> (claude mcp get gbrain >/dev/null 2>&1 || claude mcp add --transport http --scope user gbrain https://gbrain.io/mcp) && gbrain setup claude-code --instructions-only
44-> # Codex (an existing gbrain entry is kept):
--
58-> [!WARNING]
59-> **GBrain is NOT distributed on npm.** The npm `gbrain` package is unrelated and
60-> can shadow the real binary, so never run `npm install -g gbrain` or
61:> `bun add -g gbrain`. Install only via `bun install -g github:garrytan/gbrain#stable`
62:> (the soaked stable channel; `#latest-stable` is the alpha line with every release)
63:> or `git clone --branch stable` + `bun install && bun link`. Installed by mistake? `gbrain doctor` gives the fix.
64-> Schema not migrated ([#218](https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain/issues/218))? Run
65-> `gbrain apply-migrations --yes --no-autopilot-install`; if it exits 1, run `gbrain doctor --json`, not another `--yes` (`wedged`: relay its fix).
66-
67-```bash
68:bun install -g github:garrytan/gbrain#stable
69-gbrain setup claude-code              # or: gbrain setup codex
70-gbrain init --pglite --no-embedding   # any other harness, or no agent
71-```

content.text:
gbrain v0.60.760.0 is installed. `gbrain --version` reports `gbrain 0.60.760.0` (commit `1597b77`).

**What I ran:** I used the install command from the gbrain README and swapped `#stable` for your release tag:
```
bun install -g github:garrytan/gbrain#v0.60.760.0
```
Bun wasn't on this machine, so I first installed Bun 1.4.5 with the official installer, as the README says to.

**Things you should know:**
- **v0.60.760.0 is not a stable release.** The `stable` tag currently points to v0.60.753.0, and there's no `stable-v0.60.760.0` tag. That means 760 is on the faster, less-tested alpha line. I installed it because you asked for it by name. If you want the stable version instead, run `bun install -g github:garrytan/gbrain#stable`.
- **New shells won't find `gbrain` yet.** It's installed at `~/.bun/bin/gbrain` (`/harness-state/.bun/bin`), but that folder isn't in your PATH by default: the Bun installer didn't update any shell startup files. To fix it, run `export PATH="$HOME/.bun/bin:$PATH"` or add that line to your shell startup file.
- **There's no copy from the unrelated npm package.** The README warns that the npm package called `gbrain` is a different project that can override the real one. It isn't installed here, so the only `gbrain` is the one from GitHub.
- **No setup has been done.** I haven't run `gbrain setup` or `gbrain init`, so no brain exists yet. The next step would be something like `gbrain init --pglite --no-embedding`, or `gbrain setup claude-code` if you use Claude Code.
